description: Source-scoped biology and clinical context. Endogenous ECS entities are separate from plant phytocannabinoid canon.
medical_boundary: ECS biology does not establish that cannabis restores homeostasis or treats all conditions. No individual medical or dosing advice.
doctrine: RECEPTOR PRESENCE ≠ BENEFIT; MECHANISM ≠ HUMAN EFFICACY; EXPOSURE ≠ HOMEOSTASIS; NATURAL ≠ SAFE

sources.title: The Basic Science of Cannabinoids
sources.note: Foundational review of retrograde signaling, CB1, metabolic enzymes; mechanism is not treatment efficacy.

sources.title: The Role of Endocannabinoids in Physiological Processes and Disease Pathology: A Comprehensive Review
sources.note: Broad review of ECS components, distribution, and physiological associations.

sources.title: A Guide to Targeting the Endocannabinoid System in Drug Design
sources.note: Discusses 2-AG/AEA synthesis and breakdown, caveats about other targets.

sources.title: Living Systematic Review on Cannabis and Other Plant-Based Treatments for Chronic Pain: 2025 Update
sources.note: Adult noncancer chronic pain, mostly neuropathic, formulation-level clinical outcomes.

sources.title: Cannabis (Marijuana) and Cannabinoids: What You Need To Know
sources.note: Living NIH safety and indication summary; recheck prior to public medical claim updates.

entities.label: Anandamide (AEA)
entities.summary: Endogenous lipid signal; distinct from plant-derived cannabinoids.

entities.label: 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG)
entities.summary: Endogenous lipid messenger involved in activity-dependent retrograde signaling.

entities.label: CB1 receptor
entities.summary: G-protein-coupled receptor prominent in many neuronal circuits; distribution is tissue-dependent.

entities.label: CB2 receptor
entities.summary: G-protein-coupled receptor associated with immune-cell and context-dependent neuroimmune signaling.

entities.label: FAAH
entities.summary: Major enzyme involved in anandamide breakdown; not the sole metabolic route.

entities.label: MAGL
entities.summary: Major enzyme involved in 2-AG breakdown; additional enzymes also contribute.

entities.label: DAGL
entities.summary: Diacylglycerol lipase contributes to formation of 2-AG.

entities.label: NAPE-PLD
entities.summary: One of the established pathways contributing to anandamide biosynthesis.

entities.label: Delta-9 THC
entities.summary: Exogenous plant cannabinoid; interacts with CB1 and can cause impairment.

entities.label: CBD
entities.summary: Exogenous plant cannabinoid with complex target pharmacology; not equivalent to THC.

entities.label: Neural synapse
entities.summary: Cellular context for certain retrograde endocannabinoid signaling processes.

entities.label: Immune signaling
entities.summary: Biological context for CB2-linked responses; not itself proof of a treatment effect.

claims.title: The ECS includes ligands, receptors and metabolic enzymes
claims.summary: ECS signaling involves endogenous lipid messengers including AEA and 2-AG, CB1/CB2 receptors and multiple synthesis and degradation pathways.
claims.model: Narrative and basic-science reviews; variable tissue and species contexts.
claims.boundary: A component list is not a clinical diagnosis, treatment indication or claim that cannabis is required for health.

claims.title: 2-AG can act as a retrograde synaptic messenger
claims.summary: At some synapses, postsynaptic activity promotes 2-AG signaling to presynaptic CB1 receptors, reducing neurotransmitter-release probability.
claims.model: Neuronal circuit and experimental physiological models.
claims.boundary: Not all ECS signaling is retrograde; this mechanism does not establish clinical benefit from consuming cannabis.

claims.title: CB1 distribution is broad but tissue-specific
claims.summary: CB1 is particularly prominent in neuronal systems and participates in signaling in peripheral tissues as well.
claims.boundary: Receptor presence does not imply that THC improves the function of an organ.

claims.title: CB2 is studied in immune and neuroimmune signaling
claims.summary: CB2 receptors are associated with immune and inflammatory signaling in context-dependent biological models.
claims.model: Cellular and animal models; receptor distribution varies.
claims.boundary: Anti-inflammatory pathway observations are not proof that any cannabis product treats inflammatory disease in humans.

claims.title: FAAH contributes to anandamide breakdown
claims.summary: FAAH is a major enzyme that hydrolyzes AEA and helps terminate local lipid signaling.
claims.boundary: FAAH activity does not establish a universal clinical 'ECS deficiency' or a cannabis treatment requirement.

claims.title: MAGL contributes to 2-AG breakdown
claims.summary: MAGL is a major 2-AG hydrolase; other enzymes can also participate in 2-AG metabolism.
claims.boundary: The diagram simplifies overlapping metabolic routes and is not a treatment algorithm.

claims.title: Endogenous synthesis uses multiple biochemical routes
claims.summary: DAGL contributes to 2-AG production and NAPE-PLD to one AEA synthesis pathway, alongside alternative metabolic routes.
claims.model: Biochemistry, cultured cells and animal systems.
claims.boundary: A simplified pathway is not an exhaustive pathway inventory or proof of a single controlling enzyme.

claims.title: THC receptor action does not equal restored balance
claims.summary: Delta-9 THC engages cannabinoid receptors, especially CB1, and can affect cognition, memory, coordination and perception.
claims.boundary: Receptor activation does not prove restored homeostasis, universal benefit or safety for driving and vulnerable groups.

claims.title: CBD is not simply a non-intoxicating THC
claims.summary: CBD has different, complex interactions with cannabinoid-associated and other molecular targets; simple CB1 agonism does not explain its action.
claims.model: Pharmacology reviews and studies of differing experimental models.
claims.boundary: Mechanistic activity alone does not establish general clinical efficacy, safety, or an equivalence to THC.

claims.title: Chronic pain results depend on studied formulation
claims.summary: AHRQ 2025 found small short-term pain benefits for certain studied THC-containing formulations in mostly neuropathic chronic pain; pooled oral CBD-alone trials did not improve pain or function.
claims.model: Adult noncancer chronic pain human studies, specific standardized formulations, mostly short-term.
claims.boundary: Do not transfer formulation outcomes to an isolated molecule, any dispensary product, every pain condition, or long-term use.

claims.title: Homeostasis is not a universal optimization claim
claims.summary: Physiological roles of ECS components are established, but that does not demonstrate a uniform beneficial direction from exogenous cannabinoid exposure across people, organs or doses.
claims.model: Cross-domain research interpretation and human safety context.
claims.boundary: Do not diagnose an 'endocannabinoid deficiency' from nonspecific symptoms or claim that more cannabis necessarily produces better regulation.
